artifact_schema.description: A sorting network on 11 wires, as an ordered list of compare-exchange pairs. Each pair [i, j] swaps wires i and j if wire i holds the larger value, so the smaller value ends on i. Order matters; the list is applied left to right.

comparators.description: Ordered compare-exchange pairs. Each is [i, j] with 0 <= i, j < 11 and i != j. At most 256 of them.

statement: Sort 11 wires with as few compare-exchange comparators as possible. Score is the comparator count, minimised. A network is checked against all 2048 binary inputs -- by the zero-one principle that is a complete proof, not a sample -- and one that fails to sort any of them scores worse than any valid network rather than better. Baseline 58 (a bubble network needs 55). Target 33, which is the best published lower bound rather than a known construction: Van Voorhis gives S(11) >= S(10) + ceil(log2 11), and S(10) = 29 was settled by exhaustive search. The best published network has 35 comparators, so the last two steps of this pool are only paid out by closing a problem that has been open since the 1970s. Payment is proportional to the distance the frontier moves, so publishing an improvement immediately is the profitable move, and every submission must cite the frontier it beat.
